title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — October 15, 2026
summary: Active zero-day exploitation targets enterprise edge appliances including Palo Alto PAN-OS and Cisco Secure Email Gateways (CSO Online, The Hacker News), while a global coalition disrupted the Yam Store phishing marketplace responsible for over a billion scam emails (Help Net Security). Concurrently, developer pipelines face increased risk from GhostAction GitHub hijacks and zero-click Claude Code desktop vulnerabilities (Dark Reading).

tier1.title: 1. Microsoft-Led Coalition Disrupts Global Yam Store Phishing Network

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: Help Net Security

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Global PhaaS Ecosystem / Infrastructure Disruption (Yam Store)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Microsoft, alongside Health-ISAC, international law enforcement, and tech industry partners, dismantled Yam Store (Storm-3119), a massive Chinese-language phishing-as-a-service network. The criminal marketplace provided turnkey cloud accounts and phishing kits that generated over one billion malicious messages targeting 75,000 organizations in 150 countries. The coordinated action disrupted three major kits (CoGUI, Haozi, and Iron Man System) heavily used against healthcare, financial services, and IT sectors.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Audit tenant identity protection rules, enforce FIDO2 phishing-resistant MFA across enterprise accounts, review OAuth application consent policies, and update email gateway detections for Storm-3119/Storm-2990 indicators.

tier2.title: 1. Palo Alto Networks Patches PAN-OS Root RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management / Perimeter Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Palo Alto Networks released emergency updates for CVE-2026-0322, a high-severity remote code execution flaw in PAN-OS firewall management interfaces. CISA added the zero-day flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a mandatory three-day federal remediation deadline.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Allows authenticated attackers with network access to management interfaces to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges.; CISA mandated federal agencies patch or restrict management interface access by October 17.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The flaw 'enables an authenticated attacker with network access to execution of arbitrary commands with root privileges'.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: CSO Online

tier2.title: 2. Cisco Warns of Unauthenticated Root RCE Flaw in Secure Email Gateway

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Email Security / Network Appliances

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Cisco issued security fixes for CVE-2026-76519, a critical path traversal vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway actively exploited in the wild. Attackers can transmit crafted email attachments through the gateway to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Requires no authentication; malicious attachment delivery triggers file write and root command execution.; CISA included CVE-2026-76519 in its KEV catalog for immediate enterprise patching.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The attacker sends an email with a crafted attachment through the gateway and, if it succeeds, could then run commands as root.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 3. High-Risk Vulnerabilities Disclosed in LiteLLM AI Gateway Tool

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: AI Security / Infrastructure

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Security advisories warned of vulnerabilities CVE-2026-35029 and CVE-2026-59823 in LiteLLM, a popular open-source AI gateway used to connect enterprise applications to OpenAI and Anthropic models. The flaws could expose AI application traffic and token credentials to unauthorized access.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: LiteLLM serves as central API routing infrastructure, amplifying the impact of middleware vulnerabilities across connected AI tools.; Organizations using open-source AI gateways should audit external visibility and upgrade to fixed releases.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: CVE-2026-35029 and CVE-2026-59823 affect LiteLLM, which is commonly used by enterprises to connect their AI applications to providers.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Infosecurity Magazine

tier2.title: 4. GhostAction Campaign Hijacks 1,900 GitHub Accounts to Target 30k Repositories

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Developer Security / Supply Chain

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Researchers at GitGuardian reported a massive escalation in the GhostAction credential-harvesting campaign. The attackers compromised approximately 1,900 GitHub user accounts to scan over 30,000 public repositories and CI/CD pipelines for exposed secrets.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Targeted more than 30,000 repositories across 3,000 organizations to extract thousands of operational secrets.; Highlights automated secret scraping and session token compromise risks within developer CI environments.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: This resulted from compromising the GitHub accounts of about 1,900 users. It attempted to extract 3,174 secrets from public repositories' CI.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 5. Anthropic 'SneakPeek' Zero-Click Bug Threatens Developer Credentials

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Application Security / AI Tooling

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Noma Security identified a zero-click flaw in Claude Code Desktop's preview pane that allows malicious JavaScript embedded in HTML files to execute quietly. The flaw enables adversaries to exfiltrate developer credentials, including SSH keys, AWS secrets, and OAuth tokens.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Previewing an untrusted HTML file in Claude Code Desktop can trigger arbitrary script execution without prompt approval.; Exposes sensitive developer workstation keys and cloud identity tokens to theft.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A bug in Claude Code Desktop's preview pane can allow adversaries to quietly steal credentials from developers, including SSH private keys, AWS credentials, and Claude OAuth tokens.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Dark Reading
